title: 30-day Oban TTL sweep worker for channel_posts

story.i_want_to: have expired channel posts deleted automatically on a schedule
story.so_that: the coordination roll stays small and honors the uniform 30-day retention without manual cleanup

rationale: Retention is a release gate, not a nicety. A scheduled, idempotent, bounded sweep keeps the table lean and enforces the 30-day window; anything worth keeping longer has already been graduated to Knowledge, so hard-deleting expired rows loses nothing.

background.includes: Drop-in template is Loopctl.Workers.SessionMemoryPruneWorker (session_memory_prune_worker.ex): use Oban.Worker, @batch_size 1000, delete_in_batches/2 that loops limit(@batch_size) |> AdminRepo.all() then where(id in ^ids) |> AdminRepo.delete_all(), all-tenants on BYPASSRLS AdminRepo, scheduled {"*/5 * * * *"} in oban_config crontab. NOTE: the #411 MemoryGraduationSweepWorker is a scan-and-graduate job, NOT a TTL delete — do not copy it.

acceptance_criteria.description: An Oban worker Loopctl.Workers.ChannelPostSweeper deletes channel_posts WHERE expires_at < now(). Scheduled via the Oban crontab in lib/loopctl/oban_config.ex plugins/0 at a fixed cadence (mirror SessionMemoryPruneWorker's {"*/5 * * * *"}).
The sweep is bounded per run (deletes in batches with a max, logging the count) so a large backlog cannot lock the table; it is safe to run repeatedly (idempotent).
The sweep runs across all tenants (admin/BYPASSRLS repo, like other maintenance workers) but only ever touches rows past expires_at — it never deletes a live post.
The worker is registered in the Oban config/cron plugin and appears in Oban observability like the other periodic workers.

The sweep is ALERTED, not assumed healthy (issue #498). (a) ChannelPostSweeper.perform/1 emits Loopctl.TelemetryEvents.channel_post_sweep_stop/0 on EVERY successful run including a zero-delete no-op, so 'nothing to do' is distinguishable from 'never ran'. (b) A raise/DB error is logged at error, emitted as channel_post_sweep_exception/0, and RE-RAISED so Oban still records the failure and retries. (c) The absence-of-success detector Loopctl.Knowledge.IngestionHealth.detect_sweep_stalled/0 flags any ACTIVE tenant still holding channel_posts past expires_at beyond the :sweep_staleness_hours grace window as a tenant-scoped :sweep_stalled ingestion_anomalies row (reserved source_type IngestionHealth.sweep_source_type/0, CHECK widened by migration 20260722090000_add_sweep_stalled_anomaly_type.exs), raising the operator alert through the existing ScaleAlertDeliveryWorker path exactly once — with the alerted-flag ordering so a crash in the notify gap re-fires next run. (d) Recovery closes the row via IngestionHealth.auto_resolve_recovered_sweep_stalled/1 and re-arms detection.

test_cases.name: sweep deletes expired, keeps live
preconditions: one post with expires_at in the past
one post with expires_at in the future

test_cases.name: sweep is idempotent (second run no-ops)
expected_results: {:ok, ...} both times; zero deletions on the second

test_cases.name: batch bound is honored
preconditions: more expired rows than the batch max
expected_results: at most batch-max deleted in one run; remaining swept next run

test_cases.name: emits sweep-stop telemetry carrying the deleted count
steps: attach a handler for Loopctl.TelemetryEvents.channel_post_sweep_stop/0 filtered on the run's limit metadata

test_cases.name: emits sweep-stop telemetry with deleted: 0 on a no-op run
expected_results: a stop event with measurements %{deleted: 0} — a run that did nothing is still observably a run

test_cases.name: logs at error, emits failure telemetry, and re-raises on a DB failure
preconditions: the sweep's read is broken at the DB (a session-local temp table shadows channel_posts on the sandbox connection)
expected_results: a channel_post_sweep_exception/0 event with %{count: 1} and metadata error_class
the call RAISES (Oban records the failure and retries)

test_cases.name: sweep-stall detector flags a tenant with overdue expired posts
expected_results: exactly one :sweep_stalled anomaly under IngestionHealth.sweep_source_type/0 with sample_count = overdue count and last_event_at nil

test_cases.name: no stall flagged inside the grace window
preconditions: a post expired only 1h ago (grace is 6h in test config)

test_cases.name: a second run does not re-alert; an unalerted row re-fires (at-least-once)
preconditions: an overdue post; and separately an unresolved sweep_stalled row with alerted: false
expected_results: exactly one alert across two runs
the unalerted row re-fires the alert and is then marked alerted

test_cases.name: stall recovery closes the anomaly and re-arms
preconditions: an open :sweep_stalled anomaly whose overdue rows were then deleted
expected_results: the anomaly is resolved with last_event_at stamped (episode ended, suppression re-armed)

test_cases.name: tenant isolation for the stall detector
preconditions: tenant A has overdue expired posts; tenant B has only live posts
expected_results: a :sweep_stalled anomaly exists for tenant A only
tenant B has no anomaly and no detected audit entry

technical_notes: Worker: Loopctl.Workers.ChannelPostSweeper (use Oban.Worker); schedule in the Oban :crontab.
Delete via the admin repo with a LIMIT/returning-based batch (or delete_all with a subquery LIMIT) to bound each run.
Mirror the existing memory-graduation / retention sweep worker for cadence, logging, and test style.
